_guide: Replace the examples with your own data, keep "format" as it is, then upload in Savings > Import & backup > Fill from a file.
Every section is optional. Keys starting with _ are notes and are ignored.
Dates are YYYY-MM-DD. Amounts are written normally: "25600", "25,600" or "12.50" (as text, in quotes).
Accounts, categories and people are written by NAME, exactly as in the accounts and categories sections.
Categories listed here are created if missing. Transactions may also use categories you already have.
Record each account with its balance on its opening_date. Transactions cannot be dated before that day.
Uploading the same file again adds nothing twice: accounts, goals and debts are matched by name, transactions by ref (or by their exact content).
If anything is wrong, nothing is saved and every problem is listed with its place, e.g. transactions[3].account.

settings._help: currency: main currency (RWF, USD...). period.type: monthly (start_day 1-31, e.g. 28 = 28th to 27th), weekly (weekday 1=Mon..7=Sun) or biweekly (anchor = a first day).

categories._help: A plain name, or {"name": ..., "children": [...]} for sub-categories.

accounts._help: type: bank, cash, mobile_money, savings, investment, credit_card, loan, other. spendable: counts in available to spend (default yes, except savings/investment/loan/credit_card).
accounts.name: Bank of Kigali

debts._help: direction: owed_to_me (someone owes you), i_owe (you owe someone), to_put_back (money taken from an account that you intend to return; account = where it goes back). amount = what was owed on day one (optional).
debts.name: Uncle Jean

transactions._help: type: income, expense, transfer, refund, split, lend, borrow, repayment_received, repayment_made, adjustment. ref: your own short id (needed to refer to it later, e.g. refund_of). Optional on all: description, counterparty, reference, tags, notes.
transfer: from, to, amount. Optional: fee + fee_category, received (other currency) + rate.
split: amount = the whole payment, of which owed_back is owed to you by owed_by.
adjustment: amount with minus to reduce the balance; reason required.

budgets._help: period: any date inside the budget period; limit for that expense category.

goals._help: target, by (date), account (where the money is kept), monthly contribution, earmarked = amount already set aside.
goals.name: Emergency fund

recurring._help: kind: income, expense, transfer (to), contribution (goal). Repeats every N unit (day, week, month, year) from start, until end (optional). variable: amount changes each time.

expected._help: One-off money expected in or out. Use parts for instalments (e.g. a bonus paid in two parts). confidence: confirmed, expected, uncertain.

commitments._help: Money already promised from an account; lowers available to spend, not the balance.
